input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The shape check before Editor.edit_files tests only for os.PathLike and no longer wraps a plain str, so a string filename is passed on as an iterable and consumed character by character when building the editor command.
- failure path: click.edit(filename="notes.txt") launches the editor with the nine single-character files n, o, t, e, s, ., t, x, t instead of notes.txt; saving creates stray files in the working directory and the intended file is never opened.

Reviewer finding
- description: String filenames are no longer wrapped as a single path, so they are passed to the editor as individual characters. The condition must accept both `str` and `os.PathLike`.
- rationale: Calling `click.edit(filename="notes.txt")` now leaves the string unchanged and passes it to `edit_files`, which treats its iterable elements as filenames. The editor therefore opens files named after the individual characters instead of the requested file, breaking the existing string filename API.
critique: The finding gives the same mechanism as the label. The check no longer wraps a plain str, so edit_files iterates over the string and opens one file per character instead of notes.txt.
